plan.english: Friend, you have come! Enter the house, and sit down. Then eat, and drink! I give you mead, guest. May you live!
Night has come. Master, may you take good sleep! May Sky protect this house.
Dawn has become bright. Are you awake? Yes, I am awake. Come out, and see the sun!
Who are you, stranger? I am a shepherd, and my name is Wolf. Come, Wolf, to our house! Then be our guest.
Guest, go, and may the gods lead you! Do not go in the night. Sit down. At dawn you shall go.

title: The new bride at the door

plan.english: Mistress, you have reached our house. What is your name? My name is Dawn. Be dear to this house! May the fire of the house be good to you.
Guest, you are dear! The cook prepared the food. Eat the grain and the garlic, and be full!
Where are you going? I am going to the village; I seek my brother. Who is your brother? He is the shepherd Bear. I know him; he is a friendly man. Go, and tell him my name.
You have reached home! See: our son has come. I see him, and my heart rejoiced. Sit down, and eat.
Brothers, you two have arrived! Sit down, both of you. Whose sons are you two? We two are the sons of the king. Eat, and drink the mead! You two are dear to me.
Man, how do you live? I live, and the gods give me good things. And your wife, how does she live? She lives. May Sky, the giver of good things, protect your house!
Father, you have come back! Mother is cooking the grain. I carry water from the spring, and my sister milks the cattle. Sit down. I see you, and my heart rejoiced.
Great king, may you live! May your fame be great. We are your guests. Give us shelter, king.
"Who are you, stranger?" "I am the son of Bear, and my name is Oak." "Where are you going, Oak?" "I am going to the house of the king." "Go!"
"Shepherd, have you seen my sheep?" "I have seen them." "Where are they?" "They are in the field, near the ford. The dog guards them. Do not tremble in fear." "May Sky protect you, shepherd."
"Mistress, give me fire. My house has become cold." "I give you fire. Take it, and carry it home. Do not let go of it!" "May your house become warm."
"Mother, I am thirsty." "Drink the water." "I do not drink water. Give me mead!" "Mead is for men. Drink, and grow big."

"Guest, what do you seek?" "I seek a house for the night." "Where is your house?" "My house is yonder, across the ford." "Sit down; I give you food and mead. Lie down in my house." "Master, you are friendly."
"Are you ploughing the field?" "I am ploughing it. Yoke the two bulls." "I have yoked them. Lead the cattle to the spring." "I lead them."
"Father, I hear a wolf!" "Are you afraid?" "I am afraid." "Do not tremble in fear. The dog guards the door. Lie down, and take sleep."
"What is the price of the horse?" "The price is three sheep." "The price is great." "The horse is swift and big." "I give you two bulls, and wool." "Let there be a pledge!"
"What is that yonder?" "That yonder is a wolf." "Do not go to the field!" "I do not go. Let us go home, sister, and tell the shepherd."
"Did you see the bear?" "I saw the bear at the ford." "Where did it go?" "It went to the oaks." "Do not follow the bear. Night is coming."
"It is getting dark. Where is the flock?" "The flock is in the field." "Drive the flock home, and call the dog." "I drive it."
"Who is Dyēus?" "Dyēus is the father of the gods and of men." "And who is Earth?" "Earth is the mother." "Do the gods die?" "Men die; the gods do not die."
"Will you come to my house?" "I will come." "The cook prepares the food, and I give the piglet." "Do not bring a gift. You are our guest."
"Give me your dog." "I do not give you the dog. It guards my flock." "I give you two sheep." "I do not give the dog. Take wool as a reward."
Dawn the mistress stood up and heated the water. Then she said: "Hazel, carry the grain!" Hazel carried the grain. The mistress cooked the grain, and the house became warm. "Eat!"
Crane drove the cattle home. Night was coming. His wife milked the cattle. Crane said: "Give the piglet food!" She gave it food, and the piglet ate. Then Crane sat down.
Wolf built a house. He made the door big. Then he built a hazel fence around the house. Then he said: "May Sky protect this house!"
The mother clothed her son in a garment of wool. He wore the garment. "Is the garment good?" "It is good." Then she carried the washbasin to the door.
The mother prepares the food. The father sits down. "What do we eat?" "We eat grain and garlic." Then they eat.
"Sister, the sun is heating the drying-floor. Dry the grain!" "I dry it." "Carry the dried grain to the house." "I carry it."
Sister, guard the fire! The fire burns the hazel and is red. Do not let it go in the night. The fire is dear to the house, and the house is dear to the gods.
Boar the cook cooked the piglet. The lord said to the guest: "Guest, eat the piglet, and drink the mead!" The guest ate and drank. The lord's heart rejoiced.
Dawn and Moon went to the spring. Dawn said: "Moon, drink the water of the spring!" "I drink." "Our mother seeks water." Then they carried it home.
The night has come. The sun has lain down. Lie down, and take sleep. Your father is awake. May no wolf arrive at the house! Then you shall see the sun.
"Who has come to the door?" "A stranger has come, and his name is Bull." "What does he say?" "He asked: Is the lord in the house?" "Let him enter, and let him sit down."
In the house of Boar there are two horses, three bulls, seven sheep, and a piglet. In the field of Crane are a hundred sheep. Boar said: "Your flock is big. May Perkʷunos guard it."
"Brother, give me the awl!" "I do not give you the awl." "Father! My brother does not give me the awl!" "Do not cry out, you two sons. Brother, give him the awl." "I give it, and I do not cry out."
